description: Window assembler on synthetic chunk tables (design 3.3, 3.4). Inputs per case: runs of identical chunks (see the field list in README), events (every event starts a new accumulator epoch from at_chunk on), stats intervals (start_ns, end_ns, known, audible, silent, events, total, stretch; the widening and the plc rules are those of stage 3). The samples of an accepted chunk (for the bandwidth) are chunk src_chunk + j of the 'src' stream. Expected: the windows, as in the stage 3 expected files.

cases.name: gates
cases.description: One window per accumulator epoch (the epochs alternate hold, resume and route events, so the first window after each of them is observable). Each epoch is 60 non-speech chunks (label 0, p 0.02, the noise pool) and 128 speech chunks, and sets one thing apart from an all-pass window so that exactly one clause of design 3.3 decides a flag; the names say which. The window flags are the stored expected output.

cases.name: pool_15
cases.description: 15 pool chunks (label 0, p 0.02, powers 1e-6 x (1 + i)): fewer than 16, so N stays at its initial 1e-9 and the window SNR is 10 log10((S - 1e-9) / 1e-9) = 60 (just below the clip).

cases.name: pool_16
cases.description: 16 pool chunks with powers 1e-6 x (1 + i), i = 0..15: N is element floor(0.2 x 15) = 3 of the sorted powers, 4e-6.

cases.name: pool_p_below
cases.description: 4 lead chunks with label 0, p = 0.14 (below the 0.15 limit: in the pool) and power 1e-9, and 16 with p 0.02 and power 2e-6: the pool has 20 chunks, N is element floor(0.2 x 19) = 3 of the sorted powers, 1e-9.

cases.name: pool_p_above
cases.description: 8 lead chunks with label 0, p = 0.16 (above the 0.15 limit: not in the pool) and power 1e-9, and 16 with p 0.02 and power 2e-6: the pool has 16 chunks and N = 2e-6; with the p = 0.16 chunks in it N would be 1e-9.

cases.name: pool_312
cases.description: 200 lead chunks whose power grows by 3 % per chunk, then the 128 window chunks: the window ends at chunk 327, so the pool is chunks 16 to 327 (the last 312), the lead chunks 16 to 199; N is element floor(0.2 x 183) = 36 of their sorted powers. Chunk 15 (one too many) or chunk 16 missing (one too few) changes N by 3 %.

cases.name: stale_rule
cases.description: The stale rule of design 3.4: before an accepted chunk is appended, if the oldest chunk not yet fully used by a cut window (accepted[hop x windows cut]) has a start time MORE than 20 s before the new chunk's, the accumulator is reset. Epoch 1: the second accepted chunk starts exactly 20 s after the first (not stale), the third 32 ms later (stale): the window starts at the third chunk. Epoch 2: the second accepted chunk starts 20 s and 1 ns after the first (stale): the window starts at the second chunk. Epoch 3: after window 0 is cut, the oldest pending chunk is accepted[64]; a chunk arrives 19.5 s after it (and 21.5 s after accepted[0]), so it is not stale, and every later chunk is 32 ms further away: the 17th chunk after the gap is the first more than 20 s after accepted[64], the accumulator is reset there and the next window starts at that chunk (a port that tests accepted[0] instead resets at the first chunk).
